stories.event: Trilateral talks between the United States, Russia and Ukraine are scheduled in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday, 10-11 Nov, the first since February (Kremlin, 3 and 9 Nov). Russia's delegation is led by Vladimir Medinsky with deputy foreign ministers Ryabkov and Galuzin and GRU chief Kostyukov; Ukraine's by Rustem Umerov, whose delegation was en route on 9 Nov; Witkoff and Kushner are expected for the US. On 9 Nov Kremlin spokesman Peskov said the talks would be trilateral and rejected a European role; von der Leyen said the EU would be present, and Umerov said Kyiv would meet European partners (E3 national security advisers, EU, NATO, Italy) separately. Witkoff listed security guarantees, de-escalation and humanitarian issues on the agenda. The previous trilateral round with a concrete announced result was Abu Dhabi on 5 Feb (exchange of 314 prisoners). In the night to 9 Nov Russia launched 317 strike drones at Ukraine, according to the Ukrainian Air Force.

stories.event: Qatar's prime minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met President Trump and Vice President Vance at the White House on 9 Nov after visiting Tehran; Iran's two-day proposal, passed via Qatar on 5 Nov, trades reopening Hormuz for an end to the US blockade, sanctions relief and a halt to bombing. At sea, UKMTO on 9 Nov classified a 7 Nov tanker fire off Khasab as an attack; Iranian TV said 11 tankers were attacked in 10 days, and the IRGC said navigation aids were destroyed and no 'unauthorised' vessel transited overnight.

stories.event: On 9 Nov French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran's Revolutionary Guards carried out the 11-12 Oct cyberattacks that overrode refrigeration controls at about 700 French supermarket sites (E.Leclerc, Intermarché, Carrefour, Monoprix, Coopérative U), calling them 'unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression'. France summoned Iran's ambassador in Paris and promised sanctions 'at the European level'; EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said 'our response should be strong'. Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau opened a judicial investigation into the head of the IRGC-affiliated cyber unit Shahid Kaveh and two deputies and requested international arrest warrants. A second wave on 2 Nov hit supermarkets in several other European countries; France did not say whether it was linked. The BBC reported that Iran had not yet responded; the EU Foreign Affairs Council next meets on 16 Nov.

Trump called Huang 'an honorable guy' who should stay on; Sen. Cornyn called for a congressional oversight investigation; China's foreign ministry called the spy allegation 'unsubstantiated' and a smear.

stories.event: Spain holds a 24-hour general strike over housing on Wednesday 11 November, launched by the Sindicato de Inquilinas and backed by CCOO, UGT, CGT and regional unions; it is the first general strike backed by CCOO and UGT in 14 years and comes 18 days before the 29 Nov general election (El País, eldiario.es). stories.event: easyJet shareholders vote on 11 Nov at a court meeting (10:00 GMT) and a general meeting (10:15 GMT) in London on Apollo's recommended GBP 7.15-a-share cash takeover, worth about GBP 5.7bn, by Eagle Bidco (scheme publication announcement, 15 Oct). The scheme needs a majority in number representing at least 75% in value of shares voted at the court meeting, and the special resolution 75% of votes cast. The board recommends the deal unanimously; the Haji-Ioannou family concert party, including founder Sir Stelios, has irrevocably undertaken to support it for about 15.31% of the shares (Aviation Business News, 7 Aug). The European Works Council opposes the takeover and employee bodies in France, Portugal and Spain did not endorse it (Reuters, 15 Oct); no opposing shareholder has been reported. Court sanction and EU ownership-and-control clearances follow; completion is targeted by end of Q1 2027.
